title: Assignment chains resolved through a constituent labeller
summary: Statements v = c and v' = v arrive as token pairs. A labeller marks every statement with the constituent it belongs to, named by the constant at the root of its chain, so a variable can be answered at any chain length from its label. Pairs, strings and brackets use a bounded register bank with a push-down region.
core_idea: Resolve variables by the root label a constituent labeller attaches to each statement, so chain length costs nothing and few examples suffice.

state.name: M
state.meaning: Register bank of C rows, each an address symbol with the symbol stored for it; C = 64 for the listed sizes.

state.name: k
state.meaning: Number of occupied rows of M.

state.name: u
state.meaning: Holding register for the left symbol of an incoming two-token statement.

state.name: z
state.meaning: Nesting level of the push-down region, 0 when no bracket is open.

state.name: ell
state.meaning: Root labels: ell(v) is the constant that the labeller attaches to the constituent containing variable v; N_v variable symbols.

state.name: Psi
state.meaning: Learned translation from a read result to the emitted symbol, R entries.

update.plain: the labeller Lab returns, for the statement just completed, the root constant of its chain; ell(v) is set for its left variable v
update.name: label intake

update.latex: u=\varnothing \Rightarrow u \leftarrow x_t;\; \text{else } M_k \leftarrow (u, x_t),\; k \leftarrow k+1,\; u \leftarrow \varnothing
update.plain: a two-token statement or pair is written as row k of M (held symbol u, then the new symbol x_t)
update.name: row write

update.latex: x_t \in \mathcal{O} \Rightarrow z \leftarrow z+1,\; M_z \leftarrow (z, x_t);\quad x_t \in \mathcal{K} \Rightarrow z \leftarrow z-1
update.plain: bracket input: an opener (set O) is pushed, so the level z rises and the opener is written at row z; a closer (set K) pops it and z falls
update.name: push-down

readout.plain: for a chain probe the read result is the root label of x_t; for a pair probe the symbol stored with x_t (followed once more for a two-step table); for brackets the opener at level z; Psi maps it out

learning.description: The routing (chains, pairs, brackets, string offsets) is chosen by a search over the four, run on the m training items, keeping the best; Psi is the majority emitted symbol per read result.
learning.few_shot_argument: With labels supplied, Psi only has to learn the identity on the 8 constants, so m = 48 binding items cover every constant at chain length 8.

complexity.constants_notes: A row search over at most C rows per read; the label arrives with the statement. 2C + N_v + 4 words.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Routing choice plus a majority translation table over labels.

prediction.statement: From m = 48 variable-binding items with chains of 8 hops, the per-query accuracy is at least 0.99.

capabilities.prediction: Chains of 1, 4, 8 hops are resolved exactly from root labels.
Pairs routing followed twice answers f(g(x)) at T = 4, 16, 32 with C = 64.
Exact at K = 8, 32, 64 and L = 8, 32, 64 with C = 64 (state 2C + N_v + 4 words).
The push-down region gives the legal closer at depth 2, 4, 8, 16.
The limit is a storage count: C slots of two words cannot hold more than C pairs, so at C = 64 an instance with 65 or more distinct pairs loses one of them.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: This card does not compare its mechanism with others.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: No difference from earlier work is claimed.

falsifiers: 48 binding items at 8 hops after which the per-query accuracy is below 0.99.
A bracket prefix of depth at most 16 whose closer the push-down region gets wrong.

toy_example.description: Two chains of two hops; labels found by a scan; the translation is the identity.
